svg.title: For completeness, the bounded-variable inequality follows by writing K(t) = log Eet(Z−EZ). Under exponential tilting, K′′(t) is a variance and is at most one quarter of the squared support width; K(0) = K′(0) = 0 then bounds the moment generating function by et2(b−a)2/8. Chernoff optimization for an independent sample gives the two-sided bound 2e−2Mu2/(b−a)2. Apply widths two and one to the signed means and pooled clicks respectively, then union the five events.
